quote: Norges Bank should not have information about individuals' CBDC holdings or payments.
modality: conditional: only if a CBDC were ever introduced; listed as a 'rough draft' design feature
justification: The latest document lists, as a design feature, that the central bank should hold no identity information. Footnote 22 adds that it would have no 'information about the identity of individual CBDC account holders' (doc 6 p. 16). The same report says the list 'must be considered a rough draft' because introduction is 'currently not warranted' (doc 6 p. 16, p. 2), so the claim is an option, not an adopted commitment. Test case 1 also showed the central bank without access to personal data (doc 6 p. 11; doc 7 p. 8-11), but that is tested only. 'Should not have information' is weaker than 'cannot link', and pseudonymous addresses are visible on the ledger (doc 6 p. 12); the state is therefore partial, not documented.
counter_evidence: doc 2 p. 31: I den alternative løsningen vil Norges Bank eller enheten kontrollert av Norges Bank nødvendigvis måtte tilby kobling med identitet og konto

quote: Hvis alle kontrolloppgavene skal foretas av tredjeparter, må det teknisk være mulig for tredjeparter å følge transaksjoner på samme måte som med bankinnskudd i dag.
modality: conditional: if all customer-control tasks are assigned to third parties
justification: The 2021 report states that, if third parties carry out customer control, wallet providers must be able to follow transactions as with bank deposits today, including who a user receives from and pays to (doc 4 p. 23). The 2026 report confirms that KYC/AML would be done by banks or wallet providers, the same as for other payment services (doc 6 p. 16). In the sandbox, banks link customers to ledger addresses in their own registers (doc 7 p. 9-10). The statement is conditional and no design was adopted (doc 6 p. 2), so the value is an option and the state is partial. It is not an inference from KYC alone.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 24: I en tokenbasert løsning vil det ikke være noen direkte kobling mellom identitet og pengebeholdninger.

quote: Dette omfatter blant annet identitetskontroll ved on-boarding av brukere, kontroll med transaksjoner og rapportering av mistenkelige transaksjoner.
actor: PSP (third parties/banks) reporting; receiving authority not named
modality: suspicious-transaction reporting under AML customer control, assigned to third parties
justification: Customer control, which explicitly includes suspicious-transaction reporting, is meant to be carried out by third parties (doc 4 p. 23). The 2026 report repeats that KYC/AML would be performed by banks or wallet providers (doc 6 p. 16). Under the contract, suspicion-based reports held by a named PSP are a via_PSP route. The receiving authority is not named, and responsibility for transaction monitoring under the AML Act is left unresolved (doc 5 p. 14-15), so the state is partial.
counter_evidence: doc 5 p. 15: under Section 10(1)(b) and Section 21 it is unclear who will be responsible for transaction monitoring

quote: Kravet dreier seg om at systemet kan fungere uavhengig av bankenes betalingssystemer og også fungere for offline-betalinger i en periode.
justification: Offline payment capability appears as a required characteristic (doc 4 p. 8, p. 21; doc 2 p. 17), but no adopted offline mode exists because introduction was rejected (doc 6 p. 2). No document describes privacy of offline transfers at synchronisation. Under the rule that offline without a privacy description is unknown, F4 is unknown. One passage suggests anonymous payments would be unavailable offline, which points against privacy but is also only an option.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 40: dersom systemet åpner for anonyme betalinger, vil dette være utilgjengelig i offline-situasjoner

quote: For både hovedløsningen og den alternative løsningen kan det vurderes om det bør være mulighet for begrenset tilgang for personer som ikke tilfredsstiller kravene som nevnt over
limits: smaller amounts, possibly time-limited, at least one party with full KYC (doc 2 p. 26 fn 23)
justification: A reduced-identification tier is only 'considered' (doc 2 p. 26). Anonymous prepaid cards are discussed as a possibility for the closed account solution (doc 4 p. 24). No mode is adopted. Because lower-identification routes are mentioned, the §6.6a inference of F7 = no does not apply, so the value stays unknown.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 24: Siden løsningen er kombinert med lokal lagring, kan anonyme forhåndsbetalte kort gi anonymitet innenfor rammene av tillatt omfang.

quote: KYC and AML checks of CBDC users would have to be performed by banks or other market participants that offer wallets for CBDC storage and transactions to their customers.
modality: conditional on introduction; draft design feature
justification: The latest report requires KYC checks of CBDC users by wallet-providing banks. Earlier reports set access requirements equal to opening a Norwegian bank account (doc 2 p. 26). This amounts to verified identity at onboarding. It is a draft design feature for a CBDC that was not introduced (doc 6 p. 2, p. 16), so it is an option and the state is partial.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 42: om man kan holde penger i systemet uten kundeidentifisering av en tredjepart

quote: vil likevel innebære at det må gjøres koblinger mellom «tokens» og identitet, for eksempel ved on-boarding av nye brukere, store transaksjoner og mistenkelige transaksjoner.
actor: third parties/banks via identity registers outside the core ledger
modality: conditional: onboarding, large or suspicious transactions under customer-control requirements
justification: Customer-control requirements imply linking tokens to identity for large and suspicious transactions, with identity data held in external registers (doc 4 p. 23-24). Keys allowing authorised actors to unlock information under procedures are also discussed (doc 4 p. 38). The 2026 test report notes that addresses could be linked to identity, e.g. via court orders (doc 6 p. 12). All of this is option or tested, not adopted.

quote: CBDC should not be programmable money, and programmability, if implemented, should be at the payment service level.
modality: draft design feature, conditional on introduction
justification: The 2026 report rejects programmable money at the money level and keeps programmability at the payment-service level, which excludes issuer-imposed restrictions. The 2021 report had discussed purpose-bound social support only with caution (doc 4 p. 41). The latest position wins for that matter. It remains an option in a 'rough draft' list (doc 6 p. 16), so the state is partial.
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 41: det kunne programmeres inn at ulike former for sosial støtte bare kan brukes dersom visse begivenheter inntrer og til avgrensede bruksområder

quote: Norges Bank is assessing whether the introduction of a central bank digital currency (CBDC) is appropriate to ensure that the Norwegian krone remains an efficient, attractive and secure means of payment in the future.
justification: An efficient, secure and attractive payment system is the declared overarching question of the project. This appears in the latest report and in earlier ones (doc 5 p. 5; doc 4 p. 4).

quote: Introducing a retail CBDC is not a suitable measure for financial inclusion in Norway.
justification: Financial inclusion is explicitly rejected as a rationale. It appears only as an objective of the ECB or other countries (doc 6 p. 5, p. 24). No Norwegian document declares it as an objective.
counter_evidence: doc 1 p. 30: DSP skal være tilgjengelig for alle relevante brukergrupper uavhengig av alder og funksjonsevne

quote: The two most important risks in Norges Bank's areas of responsibility are linked to currency substitution away from NOK and diminished national control over the payment system.
justification: The precautionary motivation is built on currency substitution and national control over the payment system. This appears in doc 5 p. 6 and in earlier reports (doc 2 p. 6, 'nasjonal kontroll'), and is retained as a possible future trigger (doc 6 p. 7). Monetary policy as an instrument is explicitly not a motive (doc 5 p. 13), but sovereignty and control are declared.
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 7: could become relevant if necessary national control over the payment system is at risk, but this is not currently the case

quote: Uavhengig beredskap for betalingsløsninger basert på bankinnskudd, et kredittrisikofritt alternativ til bankinnskudd som kan bidra til konkurranse i betalingsmarkedet, og et tvungent betalingsmiddel som kan brukes av alle.
justification: The project is motivated by falling cash use and by carrying forward cash properties such as contingency, a risk-free alternative and legal tender (doc 4 p. 4; doc 1 p. 4). Contingency remains one of the two emphasised assessments in 2026 (doc 6 p. 5).
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 5: contingency considerations do not at present provide a decisive argument for the introduction of a retail CBDC

justification: AML/KYC appears only as a design requirement assigned to banks (doc 6 p. 16; doc 5 p. 14), never as an objective. Some authorities wished for traceability for taxation, but that was stakeholder input, not a declared objective (doc 4 p. 43).
counter_evidence: doc 4 p. 43: noen myndigheter legger vekt på at DSP utformes slik at det er enkelt å spore opp pengenes opprinnelse

quote: Introducing a CBDC can be a way to ensure access to a means of settlement trusted by all, also in new payment arenas, and can also facilitate responsible innovation and improved payment contingency arrangements.
justification: The Governor's foreword names responsible innovation as a purpose. Competition in the payment market is listed as an objective from 2019 (doc 2 p. 6-7). Innovation is one of the two emphasised assessments in 2026 (doc 6 p. 5).
counter_evidence: doc 6 p. 5: Introducing a retail CBDC is not an appropriate measure at this stage to promote innovation

quote: Norges Bank has placed particular emphasis on whether the introduction of a CBDC could promote innovation in payment services and whether it would be a suitable instrument to strengthen contingency arrangements in Norway's payment system.
justification: The latest report singles out two objectives jointly for particular emphasis. The 2018 memo named trust in money as 'Hovedformålet' (doc 1 p. 4); that is a general aim and is superseded by the later emphasis. The state is partial because 'particular emphasis' is not a formal ranking.
counter_evidence: doc 1 p. 4: Hovedformålet er å sørge for tillit til penger og pengevesenet.

quote: Norges Bank has placed particular emphasis on whether the introduction of a CBDC could promote innovation in payment services and whether it would be a suitable instrument to strengthen contingency arrangements in Norway's payment system.
justification: The two emphasised assessments map to innovation (payment services) and resilience (contingency). See primary_status for the rationale and the caveat that this is emphasis rather than a formal ranking.
counter_evidence: doc 1 p. 4: Hovedformålet er å sørge for tillit til penger og pengevesenet.

quote: The sandbox solution in this test case is based on Hyperledger Besu, which is a permissioned ledger compatible with the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM)
transaction_scope: online core (retail: Besu; wholesale: Hyperledger Fabric); bridge between ledgers
modality: platform: Hyperledger Besu, Hyperledger Fabric (earlier: private Ethereum, OpenCBDC)
justification: The tested platforms are permissioned DLTs: Besu (doc 7 p. 9) and Fabric (doc 7 p. 12). The 2026 report says a retail ledger 'should probably be based on blockchain technology' and a wholesale ledger 'private' (doc 6 p. 17, p. 19). That remains a draft and no CBDC was adopted (doc 6 p. 2), so the claim status is tested, not adopted. Doc 5 p. 10 calls the core-technology choice premature.
counter_evidence: doc 5 p. 10: we believe it is premature to draw a conclusion about which technological solution for the core infrastructure
